Respectfully
ri-SPEKT-ful-ee
adverb / interjection (Gen-Z slang)
Plain English respectfully, with respect. On Twitter and TikTok from about 2019–2021 it became a softener placed before or after a blunt remark: "Respectfully, that outfit is a crime," or "I’d never date him, respectfully." It descends from the older "with all due respect," which has long signalled that disrespect is coming. A separate playful use, "respectfully" after an admiring comment on someone’s looks, also spread on social media.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang respectfully is the softener before a blunt remark: "Respectfully, your take is terrible." Everyone knows what is coming; the word is a cushion on a punch. Sometimes it is sincere, a real attempt to disagree politely; often it is a licence to be rude while sounding fair. The Christian observation: Scripture cares about both the respect and the honesty, and the slang usually has neither in full. True respect is a command: "Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king" (1Pe 2:17). Speech should be "alway with grace, seasoned with salt" (Col 4:6), and "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger" (Pro 15:1). But a soft word wrapped around a hard heart is worse than plain rudeness; David describes the man whose "words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart" (Psa 55:21). Jesus asks for plain honesty: "let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay" (Mat 5:37). The Christian does not need a disclaimer to say a hard thing, and does not use a disclaimer to excuse a cruel one. A father tells his daughter: if you must disagree, do it with real respect in your heart and real grace in your words; and if you find yourself saying "respectfully" before something cruel, stop — the word does not make it so.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (Twitter and TikTok, c. 2019–2021; from "with all due respect") for the softener before a blunt remark — a word Scripture tests by the heart: smooth words with war in the heart (Psa 55:21), or speech alway with grace (Col 4:6).

expand to see more

RESPECTFULLY, adv. and interj. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2019–present) A softener said before or after a blunt or critical remark. "Respectfully, that movie was two hours too long."

Also tacked after an admiring comment on someone’s looks, to signal no offence. Ancestor: "with all due respect," long a signal that disrespect follows.

Plain sense: with respect; in a manner showing esteem or deference, as at the close of a letter ("Respectfully yours").

Webster (1828), root word respect: “RESPECT', verb transitive [&hellip;] 1. To regard; to have regard to in design or purpose. In orchards and gardens, we do not so much respect beauty, as variety of ground for fruits, trees and herbs. 2. To have regard to, in relation or connection; to relate to. The treaty particularly respects our commerce. 3.”

Decode for parents: listen to what follows the word. Teach your children respect that does not need announcing.

Key Scripture

1Pe 2:17 — "Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king."

Col 4:6 — "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man."

Pro 15:1 — "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger."

Psa 55:21 — "The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords."

Mat 5:37 — "But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil."

Modern Corruption

Respectfully borrows the language of honour to soften, or excuse, a blunt remark; Scripture asks for real honour in the heart, grace in the words, and a plain yea and nay.

expand to see more

The word is a small sign of a good instinct. Even a blunt generation feels it ought to honour the person it disagrees with, and Scripture agrees: "Honour all men" (1Pe 2:17). A teenager who disagrees with a teacher and genuinely tries to do it respectfully is learning a Christian skill. "A soft answer turneth away wrath" (Pro 15:1), and speech seasoned with grace can say very hard things and still be heard (Col 4:6).

But the word is easily emptied. "Respectfully" before an insult is a disclaimer, not a virtue; it lets the speaker be cruel while sounding fair. David knew the type: "The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart" (Psa 55:21). Jesus forbids decorated speech that hides its real intent: "let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay" (Mat 5:37). The Christian says the hard thing plainly and kindly, and lets the respect show in the tone and the motive rather than in a label. Teach your children that respect is a posture of the heart, not a word you put in front of a jab.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin respicere (to look back at, regard) → English respect, respectfully → "with all due respect" → c. 2019–2021 Twitter and TikTok: "Respectfully," the softener before a blunt remark.

Latin respicere — to look back at, to regard; respectus, regard

English respect — esteem; respectfully, with esteem

Letter closings: "Respectfully yours," "Respectfully submitted"

"With all due respect" — the long-standing prelude to disagreement

c. 2019–2021 Twitter / TikTok: "Respectfully," before or after a blunt line

Usage

""Respectfully, I’m not doing the group project for you again.""

"Honour all men (1Pe 2:17) — respect in the heart, not just on the label."

"Smooth words with war in the heart (Psa 55:21) are not respect."
